text: This is the word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he wrote these words on a scroll at Jeremiah's dictation, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning you, Baruch:
You have said, "How wretched I am! The LORD has added grief to my pain. I am worn out with groaning, and I find no rest."
Say this to him: This is what the LORD says: Look — what I have built I am tearing down, and what I have planted I am uprooting; and so it will be throughout the whole land.

versions.text: Say this to him: This is what the LORD says: What I have built I am tearing down, and what I have planted I am uprooting — and this is true of the whole land.
versions.explanation: The emphatic particle הִנֵּה ("look/behold") is untranslated, and "this is true of the whole land" is flat prose; the suggested wording keeps the interpretive sense of the difficult clause while reading more naturally aloud. A footnote could note the Hebrew reads literally "and the whole land, it is."

text: And you — are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For I am about to bring disaster on all flesh, declares the LORD, but wherever you go I will grant you your life as spoil.

versions.text: And you — do you seek great things for yourself? Seek them no longer. For I am about to bring disaster on all flesh, declares the LORD, but wherever you go I will grant you your life as spoil.
versions.explanation: אַל־תְּבַקֵּשׁ is a simple prohibition ("do not seek"); "Seek them no longer" adds a temporal nuance not in the Hebrew. The progressive "are you seeking" also better matches the imperfect verb.
